title: The Role of Pipe Slope in Gravity Drainage
description: Gravity is the primary force moving wastewater through a residential or commercial drainage system. For this system to function reliably, horizontal drain pipes must maintain a consistent downward angle. If a pipe is pitched too steeply, liquid wastewater rushes past solid waste, leaving the solids behind to accumulate and eventually form a severe blockage. Conversely, if a pipe lacks sufficient fall, wastewater creeps too slowly, allowing suspended solids to settle out of the liquid. Proper alignment and support ensure steady, self-scouring velocity, protecting the longevity and hygiene of the entire plumbing installation.
